canonical_definition: The Wilcoxon signed-rank test is presented in the provided literature as a non-parametric statistical test. Its documented application is to determine whether performance differences between systems, such as a proposed model and its baselines, are significant across multiple tasks. One paper explicitly states its use for this purpose, noting it is a "non-parametric test" ("ACING: Actor-Critic for Instruction Learning in Black-Box LLMs"). Another study applies this test in the context of the Tabular classification task. Across the available data, this test is consistently framed as a tool for statistical significance testing of model performance.
